independence: Separate read-only review context. Did not implement the circuit, metadata, calculations, CAD corrections or exports. Inspected the frozen sources and criteria independently rather than adopting another review verdict.
scope: Accepted 50 x 32 mm unpopulated laboratory PCB fabrication packet and later manual prototype assembly planning. This review does not accept a finished lamp, validate powered operation, qualify supplier parts or grant purchase authority.
inspected: C_SCOPE, C_SIZE, C_PROCESS, C_PARTS, C_PROTECTION and C_COST requirements and actual owner 50 x 32 decision
19-reference build BOM, including 17 electrical parts and two bare-wire interfaces
Current PCB/schematic source hashes, local library and manufacturing artifact coverage through all 202 frozen inputs
Current README, order parameters, custom T1 contract, supply specification and explicit open items
Fresh scoped spacing PASS, strict spacing FAIL and full Toolkit product release FAIL remain differentiated
Supplier ZIP has exactly seven Gerber and two drill files, clean CRC, with the optional mismatching job metadata excluded

architecture_assessment.assessment: One nonisolated buck stage, a single current-setting network, input protection/filtering, local bias capacitor and output reservoir are appropriately simple for the accepted laboratory brief. There is no unnecessary MCU, firmware, dimming, additional rail, secondary relay or extra PCB layer. The accepted size avoids further topology/layout churn solely to regain the obsolete 25 mm width proposal.

findings.finding: The principal remaining complexity is sourcing and assembly: NRND LYT1603D, a custom 180-turn EE10 coil and engineer-formed RF1/R7/C6 leads. This is not a catalogue-ready assembled-unit build, and there is no verified complete priced basket.
findings.disposition: Keep these risks visible before committing to an assembled build. Supplier/sample gauge, winding/loss qualification and forming inspection remain later prerequisites. They do not create a new copper/drill manufacturing defect in the unpopulated experiment.
findings.optional_future_improvement: After measurements and a supplier quote, compare a current-lifecycle controller and qualified stocked magnetics only as a separately checked redesign. No unverified interchangeability or reuse is recommended now.

findings.finding: Removing protection/filtering/local bypass or one discharge resistor merely to reduce count would abandon conditions those parts protect. Two independent 68 kOhm discharge paths preserve the explicitly conditional one-open discharge model; they are not two independent channels of complete fault protection.
findings.disposition: Retain the parts. The approximately 0.106 W nominal bleeder loss and approximately 1.765 mA load are now included once in the specification, rather than hidden as apparent LED current or omitted from efficiency. A lower-loss alternative would need a new discharge/fault analysis.

findings.finding: The T1 sensitivity scenario reaches approximately 108 C at 40 C ambient, above the 90 C target. Its thermal resistance and core loss are unvalidated, so neither that range nor the U1 range is a guaranteed operating envelope.
findings.disposition: The present packet correctly treats these as scenarios and retains hot measurements/redesign as prerequisites to rated powered use. Do not describe the prototype as a qualified 8 W, 40 C operating product. Do not add complexity speculatively before the actual coil and thermal measurements discriminate the need.

findings.finding: The inherited configuration retains a frameless-stencil candidate field although the current manual assembly plan explicitly orders no stencil or PCBA.
findings.disposition: The supplier ZIP/order parameters are unambiguous and no stencil is implied or included. A future process cleanup may normalize this field through the controlled configuration workflow; no rule or source modification is required to manufacture the current bare board.

scoped_verdict: No overengineering or simplicity-related defect prevents ordinary supplier CAM preview and selection of the accepted-size unpopulated laboratory prototype order. The single-stage two-layer design is appropriately simple. Normal supplier preview/quote acceptance still occurs at ordering; this review neither places an order nor replaces the retained full product/assembly/powered-test gates.
